summary: Sequoia is a language in which programs are hierarchies of side-effect-free tasks whose arguments describe data movement through a tree model of machine memory. A separate per-machine mapping specification selects task variants and tunables, so one program can run on a Cell blade and on a PC cluster.
why_read: It is an early, explicit treatment of hierarchical memory and communication as language constructs, and a reference point for later task-hierarchy languages.
main_contribution: A task-based language with blocking and mapping primitives, a machine-tree model with virtual cluster levels, and compilers and runtimes for Cell and PC clusters.
main_limitation: The authors state that the primitives may not express dynamic applications whose accesses cannot be listed as task arguments, and the evaluation covers only regular algorithms.
evaluation_method: GFLOP/s and speedup on a dual-Cell blade and a 16-node PC cluster, time breakdown, and a portability study
states_relationship_to: Alpern et al. 1993, parallel memory hierarchy model
